title: Example: Who Pays for the AI Data-Center Boom?

vocab.articleQuote: These models have a voracious appetite for computing power, and feeding them has become staggeringly expensive.
vocab.inContext: Here it describes how AI systems devour computing power — they always seem to need more, no matter how much they are given.
vocab.meaning: Wanting or needing a huge amount of something; never satisfied.
examples: After soccer practice he had a voracious appetite and went back for a third plate of dinner.
She's a voracious reader, finishing two or three novels every week.

vocab.articleQuote: As data centers proliferate across rural counties, they are straining local power grids.
vocab.inContext: In the article it means the data centers are popping up and multiplying quickly, spreading all over the place.
vocab.meaning: To increase rapidly and spread widely.
examples: Once one classmate got the new sneakers, they proliferated until half the school was wearing them.
Fake accounts can proliferate on a social network faster than moderators can delete them.

vocab.articleQuote: The rapid growth of private credit has drawn scrutiny from regulators worried about hidden risks.
vocab.inContext: Here it means regulators are watching private credit closely and carefully, looking for problems.
vocab.meaning: Very close and careful examination, often to find problems or mistakes.
examples: His science-fair claims didn't hold up under the judges' scrutiny.
New apps face scrutiny over how they handle users' personal data.

concepts.name: Hyperscalers
concepts.articleQuote: The build-out is dominated by a handful of hyperscalers — the cloud giants with the deepest pockets in technology.
concepts.inContext: In the article, the 'hyperscalers' are the few enormous companies — think Amazon, Microsoft, Google, Meta — doing most of the AI data-center spending.
concepts.meaning: A small group of giant technology companies that run huge networks of data centers and rent out computing power at an extreme scale. 'Hyper' means extreme and 'scale' means size.

concepts.name: Capital expenditure (capex)
concepts.articleQuote: Capital expenditures at the largest tech firms are expected to top $300 billion this year, much of it on chips and buildings.
concepts.inContext: Here it is the money these companies pour into long-lasting physical things — the data centers and the chips inside them.
concepts.meaning: Money a company spends to buy or build long-lasting physical assets (buildings, machines, servers), as opposed to day-to-day costs like salaries. Investors watch it because huge spending can signal confidence — or a risky bet.

concepts.name: Private credit
concepts.articleQuote: Increasingly, that spending is financed not by banks but by private-credit funds hungry for big, steady returns.
concepts.inContext: In the article, 'private credit' is the non-bank money being lent to help pay for the data-center boom.
concepts.meaning: Lending to companies from outside the traditional banking system — investment funds (often backed by pensions and wealthy investors) lend directly to businesses. It has grown fast because it can move quickly and fund deals banks find too large or too risky.

concepts.name: Depreciation
concepts.articleQuote: Critics question how quickly the companies are depreciating chips that may be obsolete within a few years.
concepts.inContext: Here it is about how fast those expensive AI chips lose value as newer, better ones arrive.
concepts.meaning: The way an expensive asset loses value as it ages and wears out. Accountants spread its cost across the years it's expected to be useful, which affects how profitable a company looks.

quiz.question: What is a 'hyperscaler'?
options: A tool for measuring very large numbers
A giant technology company that runs huge networks of data centers
A new type of AI chatbot
A government agency that regulates the internet
quiz.explanation: Hyperscalers are the few enormous companies — like Amazon, Microsoft, and Google — that operate computing at an extreme scale and rent it out.

quiz.question: Buying thousands of servers to build a new data center is an example of:
options: Capital expenditure (capex)
Depreciation
A salary
Private credit
quiz.explanation: Capex is money spent on long-lasting physical things, like buildings and servers, rather than day-to-day costs.

quiz.question: Why are AI companies turning to private credit instead of only using banks?
options: Banks are not allowed to lend to tech companies
Private credit lenders can move quickly and fund very large deals
Private credit is always cheaper than a bank loan
The government requires it
quiz.explanation: Private credit funds can act faster and take on bigger or riskier deals than traditional banks, which is part of why it has grown so fast.

quiz.question: Why does 'depreciation' matter for AI data centers?
options: It measures how much electricity a center uses
AI chips can become outdated fast, which changes how profitable the centers look
It is the name for the loan used to build them
It tracks how many people visit a website
quiz.explanation: If chips wear out or go obsolete quickly, the cost spread across those years rises, which affects how good the investment really is.

quiz.question: The article says private credit has 'drawn scrutiny' from regulators. What does scrutiny mean?
options: Close, careful examination — often looking for problems
Strong praise and approval
A kind of high-interest loan
Rapid growth and spreading
quiz.explanation: Scrutiny means examining something closely and carefully, usually to find problems or risks.
